title: tool-call-bridge-concurrency-surface: ergonomic multi-tool invocation, injection shim, and retry semantics
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: Customers building agent-style flows requested clearer, deterministic semantics for multi-tool calls, improved streaming stability when tool calls interleave with model tokens, and a minimal API surface compatible with OpenAI function-calling semantics. This PR introduces a 'tool-call bridge' and an injection shim that centralizes tool result routing, deterministic ordering, and per-tool idempotency for retries. Motivation: prior behavior allowed non-deterministic ordering for parallel tool invocations and ambiguous retry semantics which caused occasional output corruption during streaming and brittle client integrations. Goals: 1) Provide an ergonomic parameterized surface so callers can choose parallel vs ordered invocation without duplicating orchestration logic. 2) Maintain OpenAI-compatibility for function call metadata while offering richer structured-output hooks for Redwood-specific optimizations. 3) Make streaming stable when tools produce tokens mid-stream and during retry/fallback events. Design summary: - API: new optional request fields: "tool_concurrency" ("ordered" | "parallel" | numeric), "injection_policy" ("first-available" | "wait-for-all" | "per-tool"), and "tool_idempotency_key" (string, optional) to let SDKs and customers control retries. Backward-compatible defaults preserve previous behavior (ordered, per-tool). - Bridge: a new lightweight server-side component (runtime/tool_invoke/bridge.go) mediates tool invocation lifecycle. It receives tool call intents, issues concurrent invocations to the tool runner, collects results, applies injection policy, and forwards structured payloads to the streaming output path. The bridge also annotates calls with idempotency tokens and tracks transient failures. - Injection shim: converts tool outputs into structured "tool_result" frames that can be injected inline into a streaming delta stream or emitted as side-channel events. Each frame includes stable ordering metadata and an ordinal to enable deterministic replay for clients. - Retry semantics: automatic safe retries are implemented for idempotent tool calls when an error is transient (e.g., network timeouts). For non-idempotent tools, retries require explicit tool_idempotency_key or SDK-level opt-in. - OpenAI compatibility: we preserve the functions-compatible shape in the response ("function_call" and "function_result" fields) while adding a lightweight "redwood" envelope for ordering and diagnostic metadata. SDKs (python/typescript) map the redwood envelope to higher-level concurrency helpers. - Streaming stability: the bridge batches short-lived tool results into atomic injection frames to avoid mid-token interleaving. For long-lived streaming tool outputs (e.g., logs), the shim provides a "stream_chunk" frame type and backpressure signals to the runtime. - Observability: new metrics (tool_call.latency, tool_call.retries, tool_call.injection_lag) and tracing spans are emitted; Console dashboards updated. - Docs & examples: updated API spec and a new multi-tool example demonstrating parallel invocation with deterministic merge and fallback to ordered mode when concurrency budget is exceeded. Rollout strategy: feature gated behind runtime flag and a short beta period. Default behavior unchanged. SDKs include opt-in helpers in a minor release. Tests and CI: unit tests for bridge logic, integration tests against the tool runner and OpenAI-compat shim, and streaming e2e tests were added. See test notes below. Backwards compatibility: callers that do not set new fields will see preserved ordering and existing streaming behavior. Migration notes and examples are included in the docs.

release_notes: Adds a server-side 'tool-call bridge' and an injection shim to provide deterministic ordering, configurable concurrency and robust retry/idempotency semantics for multi-tool workflows. Backwards compatible by default; SDK helpers available in minor SDK releases. Observability metrics and docs included.
